A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work on Mamba's COPY operations and CoT reasoning, despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained constructions and experiments across renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic-copy training experiments and pretrained-Mamba phonebook evaluations in Section 4.3 and Figure 2.

after.justification: V2 retains the synthetic-copy experiments and reports original LIS and arithmetic experiments comparing direct answers with CoT reasoning in Section 5 and Appendix A.9.

M1.justification: The simplified SSM/gated-MLP architecture and the constructive procedures for COPY and DP solving are retained. V2 adds analysis of standard attention and additional evaluations without introducing a new algorithm, architecture, or training objective.

E1.justification: V2 retains synthetic string copying, removes the pretrained phonebook-retrieval task, and adds Longest Increasing Subsequence and arithmetic reasoning tasks with direct-answer and CoT conditions. Edit distance appears as a theoretical example, rather than an evaluated benchmark.

E2.justification: The copy experiment retains the same Transformer and Mamba comparators under renamed labels. The task-informed Mamba(2.8B)++ comparison against unprompted Mamba disappears with the phonebook experiment. The added reasoning experiments continue to compare Transformer and Mamba.

E3.justification: V2 introduces Direct/CoT evaluation protocols, LIS lengths of 10–70, arithmetic lengths of 4–7 computation steps, dimensions of 32–256, and parameter-matched model configurations. Appendix A.8 specifies 300 training epochs and final accuracy averaged over the last five epochs. The retained copy-task settings match v1 Appendix A.5.

E4.justification: Figures 4–9 add controlled analyses of whether CoT helps each architecture and how this depends on task length and model capacity. The copy-task depth, width, and length analyses remain. Removing the phonebook study also removes its targeted-prompt intervention and retrieval-length analysis.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix A.8 newly states that all experiments were run three times and results averaged. V1 provides no repeated-run count. This improves statistical reporting, but the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments received additional runs; neither version specifies confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The retained copy curves match between v1 Figure 2 and v2 Figure 3. Phonebook results disappear, while Figures 4–9 add substantial reasoning results: CoT often worsens Mamba's performance on longer LIS tasks, whereas it improves both models on arithmetic, with Transformer performing better. These are newly reported task results, rather than same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds an attention COPY theorem, definitions, assumptions, and proof establishing a logarithmic score condition (Theorem 2; Appendix A.2). It reformulates the constant-size SSM theorem, drops v1's additional explicit delta bound, and corrects the ordering of cumulative forgetting coefficients. The linear-size COPY and DP constructions are largely retained and renumbered.

C1.justification: The central COPY bottleneck, linear-size construction, general DP cost comparison, and locality-saving claims remain. V2 explicitly foregrounds attention's less restrictive COPY condition and adds empirical limitations in learning CoT tasks to the abstract and introduction's contributions.

C2.justification: V2 attributes Mamba's adverse CoT behavior on LIS to fixed inference capacity and longer reasoning chains. Appendices A.4–A.5 explain locality benefits for arithmetic and edit distance versus LIS. It removes the phonebook selective-memory interpretation and the explicit qualification that existence constructions need not be learned in practice.

D1.justification: V2 adds an anonymous code link and detailed reasoning-experiment configurations, optimizer settings, and training budgets. Reported hardware changes from A800 GPUs to four 24GB RTX 3090 GPUs, with a five-day runtime disclosed. Copy-task implementation details remain substantially unchanged; phonebook pretraining and prompt details are removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds Songlin Yang et al.'s gated linear attention work and removes several background references, including FlashAttention-2, PaLM, and The Pile. Its related-work discussion more explicitly distinguishes numerical COPY approximation and constructive upper bounds from memory lower bounds in Jelassi, Arora, and Wen.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, substantially rewrites the abstract and theoretical exposition, moves related work from Section 2 to Section 6, creates a standalone experiments section, and reorganizes the appendices. The closing Discussion becomes Limitations. These changes substantially alter the narrative and document structure.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main text, relocates Figure 1, adds a COPY/matching-set illustration and reasoning plots, and redisplays the retained copy panels as Figure 3. The phonebook panel and cost-comparison Table 1 are removed. Appendix figures combine additional conditions with repeated main-text results; Figure 9's arithmetic panels incorrectly retain LIS titles.

improvement.justification: The Direct/CoT controls and capacity sweeps add useful empirical support to reasoning questions treated theoretically in v1. New run counts, training details, and a code link also improve reproducibility information. These gains are qualified by losing pretrained phonebook evidence and introducing appendix inconsistencies, including the summation in Equation 27 and Figure 9's LIS titles for arithmetic results. Overall, v2 offers a limited net quality improvement.
